findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: There was a phone observed to be stored on top of a lid to a bread container. CORRECTED- The PIC removed the phone and educated the employee. findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There is a bottle of Sushi Sauce that states to “Refrigerate After Opening” that is observed to be stored at room temperature in the dry storage area. The PIC was unsure of where the sauce is intended to be stored and will be looking at the trainings. The PIC stated that they will discard the sauce if it is required to be refrigerated. A follow up is scheduled for 5/29/2026 to ensure that the sauce has either been discarded or if it has been determined that the sauce is safe to be stored at room temperature.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.

findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is observed to be no sealing between the dish table and the wall to the right of the dish machine. Ensure that the table is sealed to the wall and is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. The metal plate under the walk-in cooler door is observed to be loose and is allowing water to pool under it. Ensure that this metal plate is re-sealed to the ground to prevent food debris and water from accumulating under it.

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed to change their gloves without washing their hands multiple times. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC, who educated the employee that proper handwashing should be done prior to donning gloves and when switching gloves. Ensure that employees are properly washing their hands in between glove changes and prior to donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer dispenser in the mop sink is observed to not be dispensing any concentration of sanitizer. Quaternary ammonium sanitizer should be dispensing between 200 and 400ppm and the dispenser is producing a concentration of 0ppm. There are two sanitizer dispensers in the facility and the one in the back kitchen area is dispensing at a concentration of 400ppm. Ensure that only this sanitizer dispenser is used until the other one is serviced and repaired. A follow up will be conducted on 9/16/2024 to ensure that this dispenser has been repaired and is dispensing at the proper concentration. 

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: There were multiple sanitizer buckets throughout the facility that were observed to have no sanitizer concentration in them. This is due to the mop sink sanitizer dispenser not dispensing any concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- The buckets were changed and were tested to be at a concentration of 200ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are frequently tested and changed if not at the proper concentration to make sure surfaces are being properly sanitized. 

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: During the inspection, there was a metal pan containing a container of butter and a metal pan filled to the top with butter that are both sitting in a shallow ice bath. On the container of butter, it states to keep the butter refrigerated. CORRECTED- The operator moved the container of butter out of the pan and placed it in a cooler. Along with this, the operator filled the ice bath to allow it to surround the sides of the pan holding the butter to allow it to be properly cold held. 

There was two small containers of lemons and a small container of strawberries that were being held in a shallow ice bath in a metal pan. The ice bath was not full enough to properly surround the strawberries to allow them to be properly cold held. CORRECTED- The inspector educated the operator about the lemons not needing to be cold held but the strawberries must be. The operator filled the ice bath up and only left the strawberries in the pan. 

Ensure that all TCS food is maintained at 41F or less. If a TCS food is in a pan in an ice bath, the ice bath needs to fully surround the sides of the pan to allow the item to be properly cold held. 

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.
